2. The facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the respondent No. 2 Social Investment Bank Limited being plaintiff filed Artha Rin Suit No. 1 of 07 before the Artha Rin Adalat, Sirajganj for realisation of an amount of Taka 33,29,955.58 against the petitioner and another. The petitioner contested the suit by filing written statement. Thereafter on 12-6-07 the suit was decreed on contest. The decree holder bank put the decree in execution being Artha Rin Execution Case No. 68 of 2007, in that execution proceeding the respondent No. 2 bank filed an application before the Artha Rin Adalat under section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for issuing warrant of arrest against this petitioner and it was allowed. 

 8. It is evident from the record that the suit was decreed on contest and thereafter the respondent bank has filed execution case against the borrower and another. It is also evident that an auction notice has been published in the daily newspaper and ultimately no bidder has participated in auction for which it has failed. Having no other alternative the bank has filed an application under section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 praying for issuing warrant of arrest against the borrower petitioner. Section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 provides that on the prayer of the decree holder the Artha Rin Adalat is competent to award civil jail to the judgment debtor for recovery of decreed money. But section 34(9) of the said Ain very specifically imposes embargo upon it stating that at least one process for auction sale must be completed before issuing warrant of arrest. In the instant case it is clear that one attempt was completed for soling out the mortgaged property in auction but no bidder appeared to contest in the auction process.
